source_short: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2024 + JRC aluminium + China stock-flow
notes: 2050 global secondary-metal shares are analyst scenarios, not published global forecasts. IEA 2024 NZE shows approximately 47% secondary aluminium in total demand by 2040; JRC describes 60 Mt (BAU) and >70 Mt (maximal collection) of post-consumer scrap recycling by 2050, which are volumes, NOT percentages. The cited ~70% 2050 Chinese result is geographically specific. Secondary refined aluminium must have matching alloy/grade; do not treat scrap collection as market supply.

Global 2050 secondary refined-copper supply scenarios inferred from regional and IEA evidence; not direct forecasts. ICA Europe suggests ~0.9-1.0 Mt EoL scrap in ~3.4 Mt EU refined production (~26-29%); this is regional and excludes other potential recycling channels. IEA estimates of ~40% less need for new mines are NOT recycled-content shares. Copper scrap used directly in fabrication must not be conflated with secondary refined copper. Match the ecoinvent market boundary and exclude pre-consumer loops already embedded in LCIs.

source_short: IEA Recycling of Critical Minerals (2024), chapter 2
notes: IEA battery-recycling secondary cobalt as a fraction of GLOBAL TOTAL cobalt demand in 2050 is ~20% STEPS, almost 30% APS and ~40% NZE (report Fig. 2.16, approx.). This includes battery manufacturing scrap and retired EV/storage batteries; other secondary sources are excluded. Accordingly these are defensible battery-derived scenario proxies but are not necessarily the recycled input share of a specific cobalt chemical/metal grade in ecoinvent. Preserve recovery/refining burdens; avoid counting embedded closed-loop scrap twice.

source_short: IEA Recycling of Critical Minerals (2024), chapter 2
notes: Battery-derived secondary nickel / GLOBAL TOTAL nickel demand, 2050: roughly 15% STEPS, just over 20% APS and ~30% NZE (IEA Fig. 2.16, rounded). These percentages exclude recycling of nickel in stainless steel and other applications and therefore are NOT universal total secondary-nickel market shares. Do not apply unchanged to stainless steel, ferro-nickel, nickel sulphate or class-1 nickel unless equivalent recycled supply and processing exist. Figures are rounded scenario proxies.

source_short: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 (source quantities rechecked 2026-10-23) + IEA Recycling of Critical Minerals 2024
notes: Conservative 15% is an analyst lower-collection sensitivity, NOT an IEA 2050 point estimate. Base = ~250 kt secondary / 1122 kt total demand (22.28%) and high = ~560 kt / 1501 kt (37.31%). Independently rechecked on 2026-10-23 against the official IEA 2026 PDF: p145 gives the approximate STEPS-context and HDS secondary quantities; p350 gives total demand. Rounded source numerators do not justify forecast precision; the compound-grade transfer remains a low-confidence sensitivity. IEA 2024 independent benchmark: 2050 battery recycled Li supplies about 20% APS and 30% NZE global demand. NUMERATOR covers elemental lithium from secondary routes, not guaranteed battery-grade lithium carbonate or hydroxide. Apply only as sensitivity to genuinely substitutable market routes; keep purification/recovery burdens and native ecoinvent system-model rules. Existing carbonate-market share 0.000840414604538239 was read from an ecoinvent 3.12 GLO configuration and is not the global elemental recycling share. Original linear 2020-2050 ramp, clamping and higher-native-share protection are analyst implementation rules, not IEA trajectories. The existing RELICS lithium-only factors omit spodumene and cannot measure total lithium extraction.

source_short: IEA Graphite outlook 2024/2025 + Recycling of Critical Minerals 2024
notes: Illustrative 2050 low/base/high assumptions, NOT directly reported 2050 values. IEA 2025 STEPS reports graphite secondary supply AND reuse 227 kt / 11,010 kt demand (~2.1%) for 2040. IEA 2024 APS reports 2,489 / 16,023 kt (~15.5%) in 2040 using a different scenario; neither is a 2050 forecast. Do not conflate reuse with actual graphite recycling or assume reused/recycled graphite is battery-grade anode material; purification and yield losses matter. If no compatible ecoinvent recycled-graphite route exists, keep the scenario unimplemented rather than replacing primary graphite directly.

source_short: van der Voet et al. (2019), Journal of Industrial Ecology
notes: Literature baseline: 77% of lead production from secondary sources in 2050 in the cited modelling assumptions. Conservative 65% and optimistic 85% are analyst sensitivity bounds, NOT published scenario endpoints. Match refined lead market to actual secondary lead processing including battery recycling, emissions control and collection losses; do not treat EoL collection rate as supply share.

source_short: van der Voet et al. (2019), Journal of Industrial Ecology
notes: Literature baseline: 13% secondary zinc in 2050 in the cited scenario. Conservative 10% and optimistic 20% are analyst sensitivities, not literature-specific forecasts. Zinc-bearing residues, galvanised-steel recovery and refined zinc have different market boundaries; ensure the secondary route actually yields the ecoinvent reference product.

source_short: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025, magnet REEs only
notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: 20/30/39% are MAGNET rare-earth supply proxies only (Nd, Pr, Dy, Tb), NOT all REEs. IEA 2025 estimates magnet-REE recycling/reuse could exceed 30% of demand in STEPS by 2050, 35% APS and 39% NZE. Conservative 20% and baseline 30% are deliberately lower rounded sensitivities; optimistic 39% follows NZE. The immutable family key "rare_earths" may match other rare-earth markets (Ce, La, Y, etc.); DO NOT blindly apply to those. Those need specific overrides or retention of native ecoinvent shares. Also check that an equivalent recycled REE oxide/metal market with its own processing burdens exists before substitution; high global recycling potential does not prove existence of such a route in ecoinvent.

Generic analyst fallback ONLY for precious metals not mapped to dedicated gold, silver, platinum or palladium rows. 10/20/30% are NOT direct IEA 2050 predictions; the IEA chart reports end-of-life recycling rates, which are different from secondary shares of total production/market supply. Different precious metals have different uses, stocks and recycling practices. Require a real, functionally equivalent ecoinvent recovery route, not a generic e-waste substitution. Prefer individual metal rows.

source_short: IEA end-of-life recycling chart + EU PGM recycling paper
notes: Generic PGM fallback for unmapped PGM metals (e.g. Ir, Rh, Ru) ONLY; use dedicated platinum and palladium rows where available. 15/25/35% are analyst sensitivities and not 2050 forecasts or end-of-life recycling rates. PGM recycling is often closed-loop in catalysts and other industries, which may already be embedded in process LCIs; do not add closed-loop metal as a separate open-market secondary supply. Recovery from electrolysers/fuel cells needs application-specific scrap availability and recovery LCI. Do not map unrelated metal grades or PGM compounds automatically.

Fallback only for refined metals without a reliable material-specific 2050 recycled-market scenario. 5/10/15% are analyst sensitivities, NOT predictions by the OECD or IEA. OECD/IEA sources support increasing circularity generally, but not these percentages. Do not override a higher verified native ecoinvent recycled share; apply only with a real equivalent secondary production route and coherent market definition.

source_short: Primary-only market definition (structural zero; no external forecast)
notes: A 0% secondary share is a structural modelling choice ONLY for explicit primary extraction, ores, concentrates or primary-only feedstock activities where recycled input is inapplicable. It does NOT mean non-metals are universally nonrecyclable: glass, aggregates, graphite and some industrial minerals can have secondary routes. Exclude such products from this family or model them separately. No recycling credits or substitutions should be generated for explicit primary-only flows.

Observed 2025 WORLD PHYSICAL SUPPLY anchor = 1404.3 t recycled / (3671.6 t mine production + 1404.3 t recycled) = 27.666%; excludes net producer hedging. Conservative 2050 holds this observed share; baseline +10 percentage points; optimistic +20 percentage points. The increments are ANALYST SENSITIVITIES, NOT 2050 forecasts. The available ecoinvent e-waste recovery route is only a proxy for the broader recovered-gold mix, which also includes jewellery; only apply to grade-equivalent refined gold with the correct recovery burdens and no avoided-production double counting.

Observed 2025 GLOBAL PHYSICAL SUPPLY anchor = 197.6 Moz recycled / (846.6 Moz mine + 197.6 Moz recycled) = 18.924%; excludes hedging/stock adjustments. Conservative 2050 holds this share; baseline +10 percentage points and optimistic +20 percentage points are ANALYST SENSITIVITIES, NOT forecasts. The existing ecoinvent e-waste/x-ray recovery routes cannot automatically represent every secondary silver source. Keep secondary refining burdens; do not count Parkes-crust silver as secondary if it is already assigned to the primary-metal route.

Observed 2025 Johnson Matthey PHYSICAL OPEN-LOOP market supply anchor = 1547/(5557+1547) thousand troy ounces = 21.776%. Conservative 2050 holds anchor; baseline and optimistic add 10 and 20 percentage points respectively as ANALYST SENSITIVITIES, not published forecasts. Closed-loop industrial catalyst/production recycling is NOT included in these supply figures; it may already be implicitly included in ecoinvent process inventories and must NOT be added again as a market share. Keep verified secondary-refining/catalyst recovery LCI; do not assume equivalent grade for all PGM compounds.

Observed 2025 Johnson Matthey PHYSICAL OPEN-LOOP market supply anchor = 3135/(6589+3135) thousand troy ounces = 32.240%. Conservative 2050 holds anchor; baseline and optimistic add 10 and 20 percentage points as ANALYST SENSITIVITIES, not forecasts. Closed-loop manufacturing/catalyst recycling is excluded from the supply denominator and may already be embedded in ecoinvent. Keep actual catalyst/e-waste recovery recipes and grade matching. Declining or shifting future autocatalyst demand makes fixed +10/+20 pp especially uncertain; no 2050 scrap-stock forecast is implied.
